agent.problem: The distractors invent relatives for Timothy rather than using real details from elsewhere in the Bible. In particular, nothing in Scripture identifies an uncle and an older brother for Timothy.

rule.text: For who, which thing and where questions, wrong answers are real details from somewhere in the Bible, like Joppa when the right answer is Tarshish.

agent.problem: Saying that Lois had the faith first and then Eunice adds a sequence between the two women. Verse 5 says that the faith first dwelt in both Lois and Eunice before Timothy; it does not say that Lois had it before Eunice.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

human.problem: Onesiphorus appears here for the first time without being introduced, and so do Phygelus and Hermogenes on card 13. The only thing the text says about Onesiphorus is what he did for Paul. Cards 15 and 16 ask about exactly that, so introducing him would give those answers away. Phygelus and Hermogenes are not described anywhere in the passage.
human.question: When the only thing known about a new person is the detail a later choice card asks about, or when the text gives no description at all, should the new-people rule give way to the never-give-away rule? Is something like "a man named Onesiphorus" enough?
